docs.title: Accumulator
docs.text:
Accumulator charge0 · charge1 · charge2 Category Power Size 3×3 tiles

Three tall cells in a frame, three tiles each way. It holds five times what a Battery Bank does and gives it five times as fast - enough to carry an arc furnace through a night. Right-click it to see the whole network.

docs.title: Advanced Furnace
docs.text:
Advanced Furnace idle · working Category Crafting Size 3×3 tiles Input slots 2 Burns fuel yes Tube ports in, out Pipe ports 2

The furnace refitted for gas. It smelts everything the furnace does, twice as fast. Send ore by aero tube to the port on the left and take the ingots from the port on the right. Pipe methane or hydrogen into the lower left inlet for fuel. Oxygen piped into the inlet underneath, from below, burns hotter - three times as fast instead of twice, and opens the oxygen-only recipes, steel straight from ore among them. It works without oxygen.

docs.title: Aero tubes
docs.text:
Loose material and items travel between machines by aero tube — a run of open segments with the cargo flying down the middle, one cell at a time, keeping its temperature on the way.

A chest with its aero output on sends its ingots down a tube into a second chest.

docs.title: The shortest line that works
docs.text:
1. Put a tube on the output port of whatever the cargo comes from — a station, a Chest, a Grain Silo, or the port under a Hopper.
  2. Lay Aero Tube to the input port of the machine that is to receive it.
  3. Make sure the sender's Aero output is on, in its window.

Nothing needs switching on: a tube carries whatever is handed to it.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text: Machine What it does How to get it Aero Tube Carries loose material between machines through a run of segments, one cell per hop, temperature and all. made at Aero Workshop Wall Aero Tube An aero tube set in a solid plate. made at Aero Workshop Hopper An open mouth along its top, sloping in from both sides, and an aero port under its middle. made at Workbench Intake A ranged vacuum: it owns a cone of suction, aimed and switched from its own panel, that lifts loose material toward its mouth without pulling it through rock. made at Aero Workshop Fan Blows loose material away from its face in a cone, aimed and switched from its own panel with the same range and strength dials as the intake. made at Assembler Filter A tube segment that lets only its chosen material past. made at Aero Workshop Valve A tube segment with an on/off switch: right-click to open or close it. made at Aero Workshop Sorter One way in, three ways out - and each way out decides for itself what it wants. made at Aero Workshop Grain Silo Holds one kind of loose material, fed in through the aero port on top and drawn out through the one on the bottom by a connected aero tube. made at Aero Workshop Chest A cargo pod off the ship: eight slots behind a lit viewport, and eight more for each storage module in its upgrade slots. made at Workbench Destroyer A shredder that destroys whatever reaches it and gives nothing back. made at Workbench

docs.title: How a line behaves
docs.text:
• A tube must end in something that takes the cargo. A dead end, a branch, or a machine that refuses what is coming spills it back into the world — with force.
  • A full machine backs the line up. The cargo waits in the tube; nothing is lost.
  • A chest between two runs is a buffer: it takes on the left and sends on from the right.
  • To sort a mixed pile, put a Filter just past the Intake, or use a Sorter: one way in, three ways out, each naming what it wants.
  • Tubes can be coloured from their own panel — a help when lines cross. A wall aero tube is a tube in a solid plate, for bringing a line into a sealed room.

Everything for tubes is made at the Aero Workshop.

docs.title: Aero Crossing
docs.text:
Aero Crossing Category Transport Size 1×1 tiles

Lets two aero lines cross on one tile. Whatever comes in by one side goes straight out by the opposite one - up or down, left or right - and the two lines never mix. Tubes of any colour join it on all four sides. It holds nothing and has nothing to set: with no tube on the far side, the cargo simply waits in its tube.

docs.title: Aero Merger
docs.text:
Aero Merger up · down · left Category Transport Size 1×1 tiles

Joins side lines into a trunk. Aero tubes of any colour come in on three sides, and everything leaves by the fourth - the side its arrows point at. R turns it, in hand or placed. It holds nothing: when the way out is busy every line waits in its own tube, and the lines are let through in turn, so a busy one never starves the others.

docs.title: Aero Splitter
docs.text:
Aero Splitter up · down · left Category Transport Size 1×1 tiles

Splits one line into two or three. Cargo comes in by the side its stem starts at - R turns it, in hand or placed - and leaves by the other sides in turn, one payload a turn whatever it is: one tube joined and it simply passes, two and each gets half, three and each a third. A full side is passed over. It holds nothing: when every side is full the line waits in its own tube.

docs.title: Aero Underpass
docs.text:
Aero Underpass up · down · left Category Transport Size 1×1 tiles

Takes a line under whatever is in its way - a lift shaft, a machine, a wall, rock. Place two on one straight line, their striped mouths facing each other, with up to eight tiles between them: what a tube brings to the open side of one comes out of the open side of the other. R turns an end, in hand or placed. A tube joins it only on the open side. It holds nothing, and takes the colour of the tube it is joined to.

docs.title: Airlock
docs.text:
Airlock closed · open Category Structure Size 1×2 tiles

A vertical airlock, as tall as you are. Left-click opens and shuts it with anything in hand but the wrench, which takes it back; right-click opens its panel, where the mode is manual or automatic when you come near. Open, its opening is a real hole: you, sand, water, gas and even a rocket all pass straight through it. Closed, it is a solid wall. It will not close on anything solid or loose, or on you, in its opening; liquid and gas there are pushed aside instead.

docs.title: Background Wall
docs.text:
Background Wall Category Construction Hotbar label BW

Builds a background wall by the tile, in the type chosen in its own settings (Z). Left button builds, right button removes what this tool built. A generated wall is replaced, and near the surface - down to fifty cells below the ship - the right button removes it too, for good and for nothing. One cell of the type's material per tile, refunded in full on removal; free in God Mode.

docs.title: In the game

docs.title: Caves
docs.text: Caves are carved into the rock after the layers are laid, so every cave shows its own biome's rock — and keeps that rock as its background wall, which is how you tell a cave from open sky.

docs.title: Chambers and passages
docs.text:
Chambers are wide, flattened hollows; they get larger with depth, and each surface biome sets how many there are (winter and the centre more, the desert fewer). Passages are long winding tunnels joining the chambers — not everywhere, so the underground never becomes one big hole.

Nothing is carved within 60 cells of the surface.

docs.title: Ways in
docs.text: Ways in from the surface are part of the landscape: ravines cut down into flat dry ground until they meet a cave, and tunnels dug sideways into steep hillsides. There are no holes in flat ground.

docs.title: What fills them
docs.text:
A hollow is filled with air, or with lava below the lava line. A small, completely sealed pocket in a biome with a sealed gas holds that gas instead.

Underground lakes form in the basins of cave floors, filled with the biome's own liquid: dirty water in the swamp, oil in the oil sands, water elsewhere. Winter keeps none — its ice is already the rock.

Layer Lakes of Sealed pockets of Granite band Ice — Frozen stone Ice — Swamp Dirty Water — Swamp deep Dirty Water Methane Oil sands Oil — Ice caves Ice —

docs.title: Gas pockets
docs.text: Methane sits in sealed blobs inside solid ground, never open to a cave: large and common in the deep swamp, small and rare elsewhere and only deep down.

docs.title: The seal and the hot zone
docs.text:
Above the hot zone lies a sealing layer of basalt. A few winding passages cross it, each blocked wall to wall by dirt plugs, so lava and the water above never meet until a player opens the way.

Seal top 84% Seal thickness 2% of the underground (≈45 cells) Passages through it 2–3 per world Lava line 90% Below the seal Hot zone

docs.title: The character
docs.text: You are one person in a suit. The suit takes gadgets, the gadgets and the tools take upgrades, and the game keeps a record of what you have done. All of it is on two tabs of the hub.

docs.title: The Character tab — C
docs.text:
The Character tab: the suit's gadget slots, the rank and the service record.

  • Rank is earned by finishing quests; the bar under it says how many the next one needs.
  • The day counts from your landing and turns over at first light.
  • The service record counts cells dug, things built, cells set alight, the distance walked and the time played, for this world only.
  • The suit's slots hold the gadgets. A slot with a padlock is waiting for a gadget you have not got yet.

docs.title: Gadgets
docs.text:
A gadget goes on the suit the moment you get it — it never sits in the backpack. Its slot on the Character tab only switches it off and on. Gadgets are made at the Gadget Bench.

What it does Building Helper With a wall, a platform or a half block in hand, Z opens a row of shapes: a line, a rectangle, a circle, hollow or filled. Drag from corner to corner and let go to build it; Shift makes it square. X switches guide lines on and off: they run across the screen through the edges of the tile under the pointer and move with it, so a wall goes down level with what stands far away. Depth Gauge How far below the ground level you are, in metres, and the deepest you have been. Flashlight A suit lamp. L turns it on and off; switch its slot off on the Character tab and L does nothing. Jetpack Hold Space in the air to fly for a moment. The fuel refills on the ground. Phase Harness H, or its slot on the Character tab: while it is on, everything built lets you through from the side and from below and holds you from above - walls, doors, machines and floors alike. S drops you through a floor. Rock, earth and anything not built stay solid, ladders still climb and a trampoline does not throw you. It will not switch off while you stand inside a wall. Resource Scanner V sends a pulse out from you; the ore deposits it passes glow for a few seconds, each in its own colour. It recharges between pings. Thermometer The temperature where you stand, and the hottest and coldest you have been. Visor Point at anything you built and read it: what a station is doing and what it lacks, what a tank or a chest holds, what runs in a tube, whether a lamp or a valve is on. Without it you see only the name. Wrist Clock Shows the time of day on the screen, and the day on the planet in the stats.

docs.title: Upgrades — U
docs.text:
The Upgrades tab: a tool or the suit on the left, its upgrades as cards, each with what it costs.

Pick a tool, a gadget or the suit on the left; its upgrades are the cards in the middle, each with what it costs and what it changes. A level needs the one before it. Install takes the whole cost at once from what you carry, and an upgrade cannot be undone.

  • Tools get a bigger radius, harder hits, more charge and a faster refill; the Material Manipulator learns to pick up liquids.
  • The suit walks faster, jumps higher, gains a double jump, and opens the locked row of the backpack and more heavy slots.
  • Gadgets reach further or last longer — the jetpack has one line for fuel and one for speed.

Every upgrade and its cost: Upgrades.

Chest Category Storage Size 2×2 tiles Tube ports in, out

A cargo pod off the ship: eight slots behind a lit viewport, and eight more for each storage module in its upgrade slots. Right-click a placed one to open it; drag items between it, the backpack and the hotbar. Its intake is the socket on the left flank and its outlet the one facing it on the right, both at the same height, so a run passes straight through and no single tube tile ever touches both. A tube on the outlet empties it into whatever the run reaches, which makes a chest between two runs a buffer; with nothing there it simply keeps what it is given.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text: At a landed trader's terminal, Contracts lists what the corporation wants delivered: always a number of something it buys, for a reward. The better your relation, the more offers and the better they pay; they are refreshed with the restock, every 3 days. A corporation at Enemy offers only bounties. See Corporations for who is who.

docs.title: Taking and delivering
docs.text: You can hold one contract with each corporation at a time. The HUD tracks it and the Contacts tab names it. What counts is what stands on the Merchant Landing Pad: when the goods are there, call that corporation and deliver at its terminal — the goods leave the pad and the reward comes. Cancelling at the terminal costs 20 reputation.

docs.title: The reward
docs.text:
Credits — 3 times what the goods are worth, up to ×1.5 more for dear goods — and reputation. In 25% of offers part of the reward is one of the corporation's own goods. You may decline the credits for more reputation.

Easy Fair Hard Asks for goods worth ×1 ×1.8 ×3 Reputation when delivered +40 +70 +120 Reputation when failed −60 −105 −180 Reputation instead of the reward +60 +105 +180

docs.title: Deadlines
docs.text:
Offer How often Deadline Pays Ordinary the rest 6–8 days the full reward Rush 20% 2 days ×1.5 Open-ended 15% none ×0.7

Up to 1 day late, a delivery still counts but pays only 20% of the credits and no reputation. After that the contract is withdrawn and the relation falls.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Everything is done with the keyboard and the mouse. The left button uses the tool in hand, the right button opens or switches whatever you point at, and the number keys pick a tool. F1 shows this list in the game.

F1 opens this list in the game, whatever else is on the screen.

docs.title: Moving
docs.text: Keys A / D Walk left / right Space Jump Shift Run, while held W / S Climb a ladder, swim up / down

docs.title: Hotbar & windows
docs.text: Keys 1–0 Pick a hotbar slot Tab Hub U / I / O Upgrades / Inventory / Quests C Character Left / Right Hub: previous / next tab M Material picker J Hide / show the quest F1 This list F2 Hide / show the hints Esc Close / game menu Q Throw one piece Shift + Q Throw the whole stack

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Keys < / > Tool size down / up B Cursor: disc / square R Tool: next mode R Turn a fan (Shift: back) L Flashlight on / off V Scanner ping Z Tool settings G Carry out designation Shift + drag Take 10 from a stack Ctrl + drag Take half of a stack Alt + place Place off the grid

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Keys + / − Zoom in / out Ctrl + 1–4 Zoom to 1:1 … 8:1

docs.title: World
docs.text: Keys F5 Save the game F6 Load the newest save F7 God / Player mode K Spawner (God Mode)

docs.title: Mouse
docs.text: Keys left button Use the tool in hand right button Open a machine left button Open / close a door mouse wheel Next / previous tool left button, empty hands Pick up a tank

docs.title: Worth knowing
docs.text:
• Liquids are swum. Chest-deep in water, oil or brine the same keys swim in any direction; with no key held you float up, and the jump key at the surface jumps out. Thicker liquids are slower. A puddle is walked through.
  • Ladders are climbed with the up and down keys — see Wood Ladder for the first one you can build.
  • Platforms, ladders, lamps and doors snap to the grid; hold Alt while placing to move them a cell at a time.
  • A tool's size and mode are on the strip over the hotbar — see The interface.
  • Stuck in a hole? The game menu on Esc has an I'm stuck button that takes you back to where you landed.

A tube segment that counts what passes through it and gives a signal at a number you set. It lets everything past: its rule says only what is counted - one thing, a group, or everything. docs.title: The datalog
docs.text: The datalog is the game's own notebook, on the Datalog tab of the hub. It fills in as you get on, and it is the place to look when you have found something and want to know what it is good for.

docs.title: The log
docs.text:
The datalog: the entries found so far, a dot on the ones not read yet.

Entries appear as things happen: when you land, when a quest is finished, when you find a material for the first time, when you reach a rank. A new entry raises a notice and carries a dot until you open it — on the tab, on the Log switch and on the entry itself.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
The datalog's materials: every material to find, the ones found so far lit.

The Materials switch shows every material there is to find as a square, under its kind — rock, ores, liquids, gases and so on. One you have not met yet is dark. Collecting a material finds it, and so does pointing at it.

Click a found material for its card: what it is, what breaks it and what it leaves, what it turns into at which temperature, what it reacts with and what uses it. A material the card mentions that you have not found yet is written ??? — so a card also says what is left to look for.

Both lists are saved with the world.

Deepcut's shaft rig: a rotary head hung in a yoke on four legs, three tiles wide and four tall. On power it bores a shaft as wide as itself straight down, by itself - no marks, no drones - to the depth set in its window. The spoil rises into its bunker and leaves by the aero port on top; with the bunker full it stands. It stops at a liquid, at another construction, at bedrock, and at rock too hard for its bit - its window says which. Take it away and its drill string comes up with it; the shaft stays.

docs.title: Heat and fire
docs.text:
Every cell of the world has a temperature, and heat moves from a hot cell into its neighbours. Most of what happens to a material — melting, boiling, freezing, catching fire — is that temperature crossing a line.

A heat emitter switched on over loose coal: the rod warms up, and the coal under it catches with no flame near it.

docs.title: Heat moves by touch
docs.text:
• Some materials pass heat on and some keep it. Metals and lava carry it quickly; wood, ash and gases slowly. A material's own page says which.
  • Heat goes by touch. A hot thing warms what it stands against far sooner than what is a cell away.
  • Depth is hot. The ground gets hotter the deeper you dig, and lava heats everything around it.
  • The Thermometer reads the temperature where you stand.

docs.title: What heat does
docs.text:
• It changes a material into another: ice into water, water into steam, bitumen into oil. The whole list, with the temperature of each, is on Melting, freezing and boiling.
  • It lights what burns — no flame needed. Hold a material above the temperature in the table and it catches.
Material Catches at Becomes Sulphur 232 °C flame Fuel 250 °C flame Resin 250 °C flame Cave Vegetation 260 °C smouldering embers Dry Peat 260 °C flame Flower 260 °C smouldering embers Foliage 260 °C flame Glowing Cave Moss 260 °C smouldering embers Vegetation 260 °C smouldering embers Gunpowder 290 °C flame Wood 300 °C smouldering embers Wood Chips 300 °C flame Cactus 350 °C smouldering embers Coal 350 °C flame Methane 540 °C a flash Oil 650 °C flame

Ores in the rock do not light from heat alone, however hot the rock around them.

docs.title: Fire
docs.text: A flame lights the burnable cells it touches and burns out when there is nothing left; Reactions lists what fire does to each material. Fire climbs through plants and wood, so a spark in a forest is a forest fire. Water puts it out.

docs.title: Making heat
docs.text:
• The Heat Emitter is a rod that warms up when switched on and heats what it stands against. It melts bitumen into oil and ice into water — and, left on coal, sets it alight.
  • The Flamethrower throws fire.
  • A Furnace keeps its heat inside: it burns Fuels to work a recipe and lights nothing.

docs.title: Heat Emitter
docs.text:
Heat Emitter off0 · off1 · off2 Category Fluids Size 1×2 tiles

A heating rod. Switched on with the right button, it warms up little by little until its spike glows, and everything the spike touches is heated: bitumen melts into oil a pump can take, ice into water. Switched off it cools the same way. It burns nothing. Stand it against what is to be melted - it heats by touch, not through air. On power it warms up three times as fast.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text: Three things are on the screen all the time: the hotbar at the bottom, the quest on the left and the hints for the mouse. Everything else is one window, the hub, on Tab.

docs.title: The hotbar
docs.text:
Ten slots, picked with 1–0 or the mouse wheel, hold tools and the things you are about to place. The two slots on the right are the heavy slots, for carried Tanks. A tank is placed in the world, filled through the hopper on its top and taken back with everything in it — and every build cost is paid from the tanks you carry.

The strip over the bar belongs to the tool in hand and changes with it — its size, its mode, what it carries or how much charge it has left.

The hotbar, and over it the dials of the tool in hand — a different strip for every tool.

Tool What it does Material Manipulator Hold the left button to pick up loose material, release to put it down. Multitool Breaks rock, earth and wood in one disc, < / > for size; R narrows it to the pickaxe, the shovel or the axe alone, B squares the cursor. Wrench Takes a placed machine back into the inventory with one left click; R switches to painting, where a held stroke takes every empty machine it passes. Designator Designates cells. Wire Tool Lays the wires of a power network, and is the only way to see them: wires show while it is in hand. Ruler Measures between two points. Background Wall Builds a background wall by the tile, in the type chosen in its own settings (Z). Compactor Packs loose ground solid. Flamethrower Sprays fire in a cone from the character's body towards the pointer. Sprayer Throws whatever its reservoir holds in a jet towards the pointer - sand, water, coolant gel, napalm. Rocket Launcher Fires a rocket from the character's shoulder towards the pointer. Debug Brush Left button places the selected material into empty cells only; right button clears any cell.

docs.title: The hub
docs.text:
Tab opens it; the arrow keys step through its five tabs.

Tab Key What is there Inventory I The build catalogue, the backpack and the heavy slots Character C The suit and its gadgets, your rank and the service record — The character Upgrades U Upgrades for the tools, the suit and the gadgets — Upgrades Datalog The log and the materials you have found — The datalog Quests O Every quest, and which one the tracker follows

The hub on Tab: the build catalogue in the middle, the backpack and the heavy slots under it.

docs.title: Building and carrying
docs.text:
• To build something, find it in the catalogue and drag its square into the backpack or onto the hotbar. That pays its cost out of what you carry; Shift builds as many as you can afford. Then pick the slot and click where it should stand.
  • To take it back, use the Wrench — the cost is refunded only for a thing taken back or broken in the world.
  • Dragging a stack moves all of it; Shift takes a hundred, Ctrl ten.
  • Right-click a carried tank to see what is inside.
  • Q throws one piece from the slot in hand, Shift + Q the whole stack.

Pointing at a machine names it on a small plate; with the Visor on, the plate also says what the machine is doing.

docs.title: Merchant Landing Pad
docs.text:
Merchant Landing Pad idle · idle_in · idle_out Category Special Size 12×4 tiles Tube ports in Pipe ports 1

A concrete pad a trader's lander sets down on, climbed by the stair on its left. It holds cargo for the trader: materials in two tanks under the deck - any mix, up to one shared capacity - and items in slots, eight open and eight more for each storage module in its upgrade slots. On its right side the aero port takes loose material and items from a tube, and the pipe port just under it takes liquid and gas from a pump. The control panel on the deck opens its window: the cargo, your tanks to pour in and take back, and the call. Only one stands in a world. On power a call is answered in half the time.

docs.title: Lift Floor
docs.text:
Lift Floor idle · n1 · n2 Category Structure Size 3×3 tiles

A stop in a lift shaft, three tiles square, open to the left and to the right; water and sand stay out. Its deck is a platform: with the cab somewhere else, S drops you through it and down the shaft. Right-click it to call the cab. Standing in the cab, W goes to the next floor up and S to the next one down; the strip over the hotbar has the same arrows and a list of every floor, where a floor is picked and the one you stand at is named. A column carries one Lift Cab, installed at any of its floors. Wire any floor to power and the cab travels twice as fast.

docs.title: Material Manipulator
docs.text:
Material Manipulator Category Excavation Hotbar label MM Largest radius 64 cells Always carried yes

Hold the left button to pick up loose material, release to put it down. One material at a time, and nothing is kept between gestures. Let go with the square on a hopper's or a tank's mouth and the whole load goes in, none of it spilt. < / > for size.

docs.text: Upgrade Does Cost Capacity I — A wider intake field: the manipulator reaches one cell further. radiusMax → 3 4× Iron Ingot, 2× Copper Ingot Capacity II — Copper windings hold the field together a cell further out. radiusMax → 4 8× Iron Ingot, 4× Copper Wire Capacity III — A steel frame and bearings keep a larger load steady. radiusMax → 5 4× Steel Ingot, 8× Copper Wire, 2× Bearing Capacity IV — Coils in the grip push the field another cell. radiusMax → 6 8× Steel Ingot, 4× Coil, 4× Bearing Capacity V — Motors and magnets: the field reaches two cells further. radiusMax → 8 2× Motor, 6× Coil, 4× Cobalt Ingot, 2× Magnet Capacity VI — A tuned field, steered by a chip: the widest the manipulator goes. radiusMax → 10 4× Motor, 2× Microchip, 4× Magnet, 8× Cobalt Ingot, 1× Display Liquid Handling — A sealed field that holds liquids as well as loose material, one kind at a time. ability: collectLiquids 6× Microchip, 6× Motor, 8× Magnet, 16× Cobalt Ingot, 2× Display, 24× Steel Ingot, 12× Coil

docs.title: Material Store
docs.text:
Material Store Category Transport Size 3×2 tiles Tube ports in, out

One small store for the odds and ends of every material at once - a row for each, five hundred cells in all. Loose material comes in by the aero port on its left or from a carried tank, and leaves by the port on its right or into a tank. Right-click it for the list: take a material into a tank, top it up from one, or dump it beside the store. Its outlet is off until you switch it on, and then sends everything row by row - a sorter down the line tells them apart. Water poured in from a tank leaves only by a tank. It cannot be upgraded.

docs.title: A new world
docs.text: New World in the main menu asks for a name, a size and a seed. The same size and seed always make the same world — the sizes are compared on The world. Every world starts with the same hotbar: the Material Manipulator, the Multitool and two empty Tanks.

docs.title: Player Mode and God Mode
docs.text:
F7 switches between them at any time.

Player Mode God Mode Building costs what the catalogue says free Moving walking, jumping, swimming, the jetpack on its fuel free flight Tools the flamethrower's tank runs dry, rockets come back one at a time no limits, any radius The scanner recharges between pings no recharge The datalog shows what you have found shows everything The service record counts paused

God Mode also has the spawner on K, which hands out any item, and lets the Designator carry out what it marked.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
• F5 saves the world, and so does Save in the game menu on Esc.
  • F6 loads the newest save. Load in the main menu lists every saved world.
  • The game saves by itself every few minutes; how often is set under Settings → Game.

A save holds the whole world as it stands — every cell with its temperature, every machine with what it holds and what it was doing, your inventory, quests, upgrades and datalog.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings, from the game menu on Esc.

Settings is in the main menu and in the game menu. Graphics has the resolution and fullscreen; Game has the autosave interval and whether a new world starts with the tutorial quests. A change applies at once; Save keeps it, and leaving without saving puts things back.

docs.title: Pipes and pumps
docs.text:
Liquids and gases are moved by pipe. A pipe carries nothing by itself: something has to push at one end and something has to take at the other.

A pump standing in a pool lifts the water through a pipe into a liquid tank.

docs.title: The shortest line that works
docs.text:
1. Stand a Pump in the liquid it is to pump — it draws from the cells beside it.
  2. Lay Pipe from the pump to where the liquid should go. Segments join by touching and take the shape of the run.
  3. End the run in an Outlet, which pours the liquid back into the world from the grate on its underside, or in a Liquid Tank, which keeps it.
  4. Right-click the pump to switch it on.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text: Machine What it does How to get it Pipe A pipe segment. made at Pipe Workshop Wall Pipe A pipe set in a solid plate. made at Pipe Workshop Pump Draws liquid from a cell beside it and pushes it through connected pipes to an outlet. made at Pipe Workshop Outlet Returns liquid from the pipe network to the world as an ordinary cell, pouring from the grate on its underside. made at Pipe Workshop Pipe Valve A pipe segment with a lever: right-click to open or shut it. made at Pipe Workshop Liquid Tank Holds one kind of liquid, piped in through the port on its left and sent on through the port on its right as if a pump stood inside it. made at Pipe Workshop Gas Pump Draws gas from the cells around it, the highest first, and pushes it through connected pipes to a gas vent or an accepting gas tank. made at Pipe Workshop Gas Vent Returns gas from the pipe network to the world as an ordinary cell, pouring from the grate on its top. made at Pipe Workshop Gas Tank Holds one kind of gas, piped in through the port on its left and sent on through the port on its right as if a gas pump stood inside it. made at Pipe Workshop

docs.title: How a line behaves
docs.text:
• A covered outlet stops the flow. Flood the grate or fill the container under it and the pump waits — nothing overflows.
  • A tank takes one kind. A pump fills a tank only while it is empty or holds the same liquid with room to spare; otherwise it moves on to the next target on the run.
  • A tank pumps onward by itself. What comes in through the port on its left leaves through the port on its right, so tanks can stand in a row.
  • A shut valve loses nothing. The pump behind it simply stops drawing.
  • Gas uses the same pipes but its own ends: a Gas Pump draws it in, a Gas Vent lets it out, a Gas Tank keeps it. Fire is never drawn in.
  • A wall pipe is a pipe in a solid plate: lay it in a wall to bring a line into a sealed room.

Stations take liquid by pipe too — the Water Purifier, the Washer and the Still all have a pipe port. To carry a liquid by hand it has to be canned at the Canister Filler.

docs.title: Plants
docs.text: Plants are placed when the world is made and grow nowhere else afterwards: they root in turf, hang from cave ceilings or stand on cave floors.

docs.title: Turf
docs.text: The top of every exposed soil column becomes turf — grassy dirt in the centre, lichen in winter. Surface plants root in turf and nothing else, so bare soil you dig out grows nothing.

docs.title: Vines and grass
docs.text:
A vine grows away from what holds it: up from the ground, down from a ceiling. It is one cell wide and never grows diagonally, so fire runs along it cell by cell.

Plant Grows up to Where Icicle 6 cells Icicles, hanging from permafrost and ice. Vegetation 5 cells Grass and flowers on turf, outdoors only. Cave Vegetation 8 cells Cave vines, hanging from the ceilings of caves under every rock. Glowing Cave Moss 8 cells A glowing cave vine, which can end in a glowing cave flower. Cave Moss 3 cells Low moss on cave floors, thickest in the swamp and the grottos. Mushroom Stem 6 cells The stem of a mushroom, standing on a cave floor. Root 14 cells Roots hanging from dirt and clay ceilings. Cactus 6 cells Cactus, on the desert's sand. Wood 80 cells Tree trunks and branches. Foliage 5 cells Leaves, the crown of a tree or a bush.

Polymeriser Category Crafting Size 2×3 tiles Input slots 1 Burns fuel no Tube ports out Pipe ports 1

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: 62 quests teach the game one step at a time; most open a station when they are done, and finishing them raises your rank. They come in chains — each below says what it follows.

docs.title: Salvage
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Salvage
docs.text:
The ship came down in one piece, nearly. One locker in it stayed shut through the crash - whatever survived is in there.

  1. Right-click the ship's locker and take what it holds. — have Material Manipulator; have Multitool

The manipulator, the multitool, two tanks and a flashlight - fit it on the Character tab, and L lights the way.

docs.title: Dig In … Plate by Plate
docs.text: After Salvage.

docs.title: Dig In
docs.text:
The Material Manipulator picks up loose material, but the ground is solid. Break it loose with the Multitool first, then gather what falls.

  1. Dig with the Multitool (2), then pick the dirt up with the Manipulator (1). — carry 20 cells of Loose Dirt

Loose material goes wherever you put it down. The manipulator carries one material at a time.

docs.title: Fill a Tank
docs.text:
Tanks hold loose material. Place one from a heavy slot and pour dirt in through the hopper on top.

  1. Place a Tank from a heavy slot. — build Tank
  2. Pour loose dirt into it through the hopper. — store 100 cells of Loose Dirt

A tank keeps what you pour into it, and it travels with its contents.

docs.title: Take It With You
docs.text:
A full tank goes back into a heavy slot, and the material goes with you. Building spends what your carried tanks hold.

  1. Pick an empty slot and click the tank to take it back. — have 100 cells of Loose Dirt

Carried tanks are your materials: every build cost is paid from them.

docs.title: Before the Mine
docs.text:
Ore is under the ground, and a shaft is a long way down in the dark. The ship's hold still has what a miners' shuttle carries for that: ladders and lamps.

  1. Right-click the Ship's Storage - the crates in the hold by the stern - and take the ladders and the lamps. — have 10× Wood Ladder; have 2× Lamp

A ladder goes down a tile at a time, and a lamp lights the rock round it. Both are placed from the bar like any construction.

docs.title: A Ladder of Your Own
docs.text:
Ten ladders reach ten metres, and the ore goes deeper. A Wood Ladder is made of wood chips: fell a tree with the Multitool, gather the chips, and build as many as the shaft needs.

  1. Fell a tree with the Multitool (2) and collect the Wood Chips in a tank. — have 20 cells of Wood Chips
  2. Open the hub (Tab): in the Catalogue, drag a Wood Ladder to the bar - it is built there - then place it. — build 2× Wood Ladder

A construction made of loose material is built this way: the material in a carried tank, then a drag to the bar.

docs.title: Build a Furnace
docs.text:
A furnace turns ore into ingots. It is built from loose clay and loose dirt - dig both, collect each in a tank of its own, and place the furnace.

  1. Collect loose clay and loose dirt, each in a tank. — have 144 cells of Loose Clay; have 60 cells of Loose Dirt
  2. Place a Furnace. — build Furnace

Opens: Furnace

The furnace smelts ore into ingots. Open it and give it ore and fuel.

docs.title: First Melt
docs.text:
The furnace fires clay into brick and smelts ore into ingots. A workbench needs both - and after it, the real making starts.

  1. Fire bricks and smelt iron in the furnace. — have 8× Brick; have 2× Iron Ingot
  2. Place a Workbench. — build Workbench

Opens: Workbench

The workbench forges plates, pipes and bearings from ingots.

docs.title: Plate by Plate
docs.text:
Every machine of the camp starts with iron plate, and many with a bearing. Forge a stock of both at the workbench.

  1. Forge iron plates and bearings at the workbench. — have 6× Iron Plate; have 2× Bearing

Two roads open from here: the soil and the metal. Follow either - or both.

docs.title: Locker Two
docs.text: After Plate by Plate.

docs.title: Locker Two
docs.text:
The second locker in the ship's hold took a dent and will not open. Iron plate and copper wire would put it right, both made at the workbench. What is inside is worth it.

  1. Repair the second locker at the console by the hatch, then right-click it and take what it holds. — have Flamethrower

A flamethrower and a wrench: fire to dry what is wet, and machines that can be moved.

docs.title: Air Works
docs.text: After Plate by Plate.

docs.title: Air Works
docs.text:
Every ingot the furnace pours is carried to the workbench by hand. Aero tubes carry it by air from one machine's port to the next. The aero workshop makes the tubes, intakes and valves, all out of iron.

  1. Build an Aero Workshop from hull plates, iron pipe and bearings made at the workbench. — build Aero Workshop

Opens: Aero Workshop

The workshop is up. Next, the tubes it makes - and something to blow down them.

docs.title: Tubes and a Fan … Into the Silo
docs.text: After Air Works.

docs.title: Tubes and a Fan
docs.text:
A tube carries what something blows into it. An intake is a fan in a hood: set it by loose ground and it pulls the grains in and sends them down the tube.

  1. Make a Machine Fan at the workbench - a bearing and fan blades. — have Machine Fan
  2. At the Aero Workshop make an Aero Intake from the fan, iron and copper ingots, and eight Aero Tubes from iron pipe. — have Intake; have 8× Aero Tube

Eight tubes and an intake. All that is missing is somewhere for it to go.

docs.title: Into the Silo
docs.text:
A Grain Silo holds loose ground by the thousand cells and takes it in at the top. Run the intake's tube to it and the digging carries itself home.

  1. Make a Grain Silo at the Aero Workshop - hull plates and glass, smelted from sand in the furnace - and set it down. — stand Grain Silo
  2. Set the intake on loose ground - sand, dirt - and lay tubes from its port to the silo's intake on top. Let it run. — deliver 200× Grain Silo

The ground comes in by itself now. Every machine with a port can be fed the same way.

docs.title: Running Water
docs.text: After Into the Silo.

docs.title: Running Water
docs.text:
Carrying water by the tank is slow. The pipe workshop makes pipes and pumps: put a pump in water and pipe it to where it is needed.

  1. Place a Pipe Workshop. — build Pipe Workshop
  2. Lay a pump and a run of pipe. — build Pump; build 4× Pipe

Opens: Pipe Workshop

A pump in a pool and a pipe to a station: water that comes by itself.

docs.title: Full Circle … Garden Under Glass
docs.text: After Running Water.

docs.title: Full Circle
docs.text:
Nothing here goes to waste. A composter rots leaves and petals into biomass - the seed stock of a garden, the same that mown grass gives - and biomass and ash into loose dirt.

  1. Place a Composter. — build Composter
  2. Cut grass and gather the biomass it leaves. — have 20 cells of Biomass

Opens: Composter

Biomass and water are all a plant needs - given somewhere to grow.

docs.title: Garden Under Glass
docs.text:
An incubator grows wood, leaves and flowers from biomass and water. Pipe the water in.

  1. Place a Plant Incubator. — build Plant Incubator
  2. Grow wood in it. — have 40 cells of Wood Chips

Opens: Plant Incubator

Grown wood, grown petals: the garden pays back what it is given.

docs.title: Grind It Down
docs.text: After Plate by Plate.

docs.title: Grind It Down
docs.text:
A crusher grinds coal and iron to dust, petals to dye and wood to paper.

  1. Place a Crusher. — build Crusher
  2. Crush coal and iron to dust. — have 4× Coal Dust; have 4× Iron Dust

Opens: Crusher

Iron dust and coal dust, mixed, are the start of steel.

docs.title: Mix It Up
docs.text: After Grind It Down.

docs.title: Mix It Up
docs.text:
A mixer tumbles dusts together. Iron and coal make steel dust; sulphur and coal make gunpowder.

  1. Place a Mixer. — build Mixer
  2. Mix iron dust and coal dust into steel dust. — have 10 cells of Steel Dust

Opens: Mixer

Steel dust smelts into steel in the furnace.

docs.title: Walls and Doors
docs.text: After Plate by Plate.

docs.title: Walls and Doors
docs.text:
A camp needs walls that stay where they are put. The fabricator makes walls, ramps, ladders and doors.

  1. Place a Fabricator. — build Fabricator
  2. Make a door and set it in a wall. — build Iron Door

Opens: Fabricator

Walls keep the loose ground out - and doors let you back in.

docs.title: Coloured Light
docs.text: After Garden Under Glass, Grind It Down.

docs.title: Coloured Light
docs.text:
Lilac flowers grow on the surface. Ground to dust in the crusher, a petal tints glass at the workbench - and tinted glass in a lamp colours its light.

  1. Tint a pane of glass with lilac petal dust. — have Lilac Glass
  2. Place a lamp and fit the glass from its panel. — build Lamp

Any petal tints glass. The night here does not have to be one colour.

docs.title: Steel
docs.text: After Mix It Up, Running Water, Garden Under Glass, Into the Silo.

docs.title: Steel
docs.text:
Steel is what the rest of the base is built from. Smelt steel dust into ingots in the furnace and forge plates at the workbench.

  1. Forge steel plates. — have 4× Steel Plate

With steel, the rest of the ship's manifest can be built.

docs.title: More Room
docs.text: After Steel.

docs.title: More Room
docs.text:
A chest holds one row. A storage module in one of its upgrade slots opens another, up to three modules a chest. The Ship's Storage takes modules the same way.

  1. Make a storage module at the workbench from steel plates and bearings. — have Storage Module
  2. Put it in an upgrade slot - a chest's, or the Ship's Storage's. — fit Storage Module

Each module opens a row of eight. It comes out again only while that row is empty.

docs.title: Locker Three
docs.text: After Steel.

docs.title: Locker Three
docs.text:
The third locker, in the crew deck, burnt in the crash. Steel plate and a pane of glass would make it whole again.

  1. Repair the third locker at the console by the hatch, then right-click it and take what it holds. — have Sprayer

The Background Wall and the sprayer: walls behind the machines you build, and liquid where you aim it. And a ruler, to count the tiles between two places before you build across them.

docs.title: Clean Water
docs.text: After Steel.

docs.title: Clean Water
docs.text:
Water from the caves, and from the washer, is dirty. A purifier filters it clean through a cartridge of coal dust and paper.

  1. Place a Water Purifier. — build Water Purifier
  2. Pack filter cartridges at the workbench. — have 2× Filter Cartridge

Opens: Water Purifier

Clean water: for the garden, the washer and the machines to come.

docs.title: Pan for Ore
docs.text: After Steel.

docs.title: Pan for Ore
docs.text:
Washed with water, any common ground gives up a little ore concentrate - the raw stock of everything rare.

  1. Place a Washer. — build Washer
  2. Wash ground into ore concentrate. — have 20 cells of Ore Concentrate

Opens: Washer

Concentrate holds more than the veins show. Something will have to sort it.

docs.title: Thinking Machines
docs.text: After Clean Water, Pan for Ore.

docs.title: Thinking Machines
docs.text:
Silicon ore smelts into wafers in the furnace; the assembler makes wafers and copper into chips, and chips, coils and plate into motors.

  1. Place an Assembler. — build Assembler
  2. Assemble microchips and a motor. — have 2× Microchip; have Motor

Opens: Assembler

Chips and motors: the last machines on the manifest can be built.

docs.title: Every Grain Its Place
docs.text: After Air Works, Thinking Machines.

docs.title: Every Grain Its Place
docs.text:
One tube carries whatever is put into it, all mixed together. A sorter reads what passes and sends each material and each item down the side that asked for it. It takes microchips and a display, so it waited for the assembler.

  1. Make a Sorter at the Aero Workshop and place it on a tube line. — build Sorter

One line in, three lines out, each with its own cargo: the camp sorts itself.

docs.title: Listening … A Place to Land
docs.text: After Thinking Machines.

docs.title: Listening
docs.text:
The mast on the ship's hump was sheared off in the crash. Copper wire and a pair of microchips would put it back - and with it, an ear on the sky.

  1. Repair the antenna - Navigation's first tier - at the ship's console. — repair Navigation

Someone is out there: traders' beacons, and a call sign for anyone with somewhere to land.

docs.title: A Place to Land
docs.text:
A trader's lander needs flat ground it can trust under open sky. A landing pad gives it that, and holds the cargo you mean to trade.

  1. Place a Merchant Landing Pad under open sky. — build Merchant Landing Pad

Opens: Merchant Landing Pad

The pad stands ready. Its panel will call a trader as soon as one answers.

docs.title: Under Pressure
docs.text: After Thinking Machines.

docs.title: Under Pressure
docs.text:
A compressor packs loose material into blocks - a tank's worth carried in one slot.

  1. Place a Compressor. — build Compressor
  2. Compress iron ore into blocks. — have 2× Compressed Iron

Opens: Compressor

Packed tight, a block travels light.

docs.title: Sorting the Grains
docs.text: After Thinking Machines.

docs.title: Sorting the Grains
docs.text:
Ore concentrate holds more than stone. A separator sorts it grain by grain - mostly stone, sometimes copper or silicon, rarely gold or platinum.

  1. Place a Separator. — build Separator
  2. Sort concentrate until you have silicon. — have 10 cells of Raw Silicon

Opens: Separator

Keep it running. The rarest grains come one in a thousand draws, or fewer.

docs.title: Set in Stone
docs.text: After Thinking Machines.

docs.title: Set in Stone
docs.text:
Sand, stone and ash with water make concrete. Pour it wet into a form of walls and let it set; broken up, it gives loose concrete back.

  1. Place a Concrete Mixer. — build Concrete Mixer
  2. Pour concrete, let it set, and break it loose. — have 20 cells of Concrete Rubble

Opens: Concrete Mixer

Loose concrete becomes walls, ramps and ladders at the fabricator.

docs.title: Instruments … Refinery
docs.text: After Thinking Machines.

docs.title: Instruments
docs.text:
The suit has slots for instruments the ship no longer carries. The gadget bench makes them - start with the two that read the ground.

  1. Place a Gadget Bench. — build Gadget Bench
  2. Make a thermometer and a depth gauge. — have Thermometer; have Depth Gauge

Opens: Gadget Bench

Deep down, where the rock is hot, something lies that burns.

docs.title: By the Canister
docs.text:
A liquid will not go into a tank you carry. A canister holds a hundred cells of it: a filler takes liquid from a pipe and an empty canister and gives a full one, and an extractor pours a full one back into a pipe.

  1. Place a Canister Filler and pipe water into it. — build Canister Filler
  2. Make a canister at the workbench. — have Empty Canister
  3. Put the canister into the filler and fill it with water. — have Water Canister
  4. Place a Canister Extractor, with a pipe from it to a liquid tank. — build Canister Extractor
  5. Put the full canister into the extractor and empty it. — run Canister Extractor

Opens: Canister Filler, Canister Extractor

Any liquid, and any gas, can now be carried by hand. Deep down, something waits to be carried.

docs.title: Black Gold
docs.text:
Bitumen lies deep, in the hot layers. Heated past its melting point it runs as oil. Gather it in a liquid tank, and fill a canister to carry it up.

  1. Melt bitumen into oil, pipe it to a Canister Filler and fill a canister. — have Oil Canister

Oil burns - and distilled, it gives something cleaner.

docs.title: Refinery
docs.text:
A still distils oil into fuel, and gives off methane as it does. Fuel burns hot in any furnace, and it can be carried in canisters.

  1. Place a Still. — build Still
  2. Distil oil into fuel and store it in a liquid tank. — store 50 cells of Fuel

Opens: Still

Fuel in the tank, methane off the top. Both burn - and the methane can be put to work.

docs.title: Plastics … Locker Four
docs.text: After Refinery.

docs.title: Plastics
docs.text:
The still's methane need not be wasted. Over a platinum catalyst, hot, it joins into plastic - and plastic insulates the wiring the finest instruments need.

  1. Place a Polymeriser and pipe methane into it. — build Polymeriser
  2. Make plastic, and insulate wire with it at the assembler. — have 2× Insulated Wire

Opens: Polymeriser

Insulated wire: the instruments and the suit's last upgrades take it.

docs.title: Locker Four
docs.text:
The fourth locker, up in the hump over the crew deck, took a blow that crushed its corner and killed the chip in its lock. New microchips will wake it, and insulated wire - plastic over copper, which the assembler makes now there is plastic.

  1. Repair the fourth locker at the console by the hatch, then right-click it and take what it holds. — have Designator

Opens: Electrics Bench

The designator: mark the ground, and it is cleared for you. And a Wire Tool - with an Electrics Bench to build what the wires will join.

docs.title: Gas Lines
docs.text: After Refinery.

docs.title: Gas Lines
docs.text:
The still gives off methane as it parts the oil. Gas runs through the same pipes as water, but it needs a pump of its own to draw it and a tank of its own to hold it.

  1. Place a Gas Pump and a Gas Tank. — build Gas Pump; build Gas Tank
  2. Pipe the still's methane into the gas tank. — store 50 cells of Methane

Opens: Scrubber

Methane in a tank, under pressure. Anything that burns clean can burn this.

docs.title: Split Water … Tanks Full
docs.text: After Gas Lines, Locker Four.

docs.title: Split Water
docs.text:
Pure water, pulled apart in an electrolyser, gives hydrogen, the lightest fuel there is, and oxygen beside it. It is power that pulls it apart: the electrolyser burns nothing and stands still until it is wired to a battery bank or a panel.

  1. Place an Electrolyser and wire it to a Battery Bank with the Wire Tool. — build Electrolyser
  2. Split water and store the hydrogen in a gas tank. — store 50 cells of Hydrogen

Opens: Electrolyser, Condenser, Electric Furnace, Boiler, Steam Turbine

Hydrogen, from nothing but water. The ship's tank has been waiting for exactly this.

docs.title: Blue Flame
docs.text:
A furnace on gas runs twice as fast. With oxygen piped in underneath it runs faster still, hot enough to turn iron ore and coal straight into steel.

  1. Place an Advanced Furnace. Pipe methane or hydrogen into its left inlet and oxygen into the inlet underneath. — build Advanced Furnace
  2. Pipe the electrolyser's oxygen into a gas tank - the furnace draws its oxygen from there. — store 50 cells of Oxygen
  3. Make steel from iron ore and coal in oxygen. — have 10× Steel Ingot

Opens: Advanced Furnace, Autoclave, Fuel Cell

Steel straight from the ore, in a flame that is almost invisible.

docs.title: Tanks Full
docs.text:
The ship's tanks take gas through the inlet on its hull. Hydrogen for the engine, oxygen to burn it with: pump both in until the tanks are full.

  1. Pump hydrogen into the ship's hydrogen tank - built once Fuel is repaired. — fill 2000 cells of Hydrogen
  2. Pump oxygen into the ship's oxygen tank - built once the Oxidiser is repaired. — fill 1000 cells of Oxygen

Both tanks full. The engine has everything it needs but a way off the ground.

docs.title: Sap and Sulphur … Leap of Faith
docs.text: After Refinery.

docs.title: Sap and Sulphur
docs.text:
The ship's fuel lines and air loop need seals that give. Resin comes from felled trunks now and then, or grown in the incubator from wood, biomass and water; sulphur lies in the yellow veins.

  1. Gather resin and sulphur, each in a tank. — have 20 cells of Resin; have 10 cells of Sulphur

Resin and sulphur, fired together, make rubber.

docs.title: Vulcanised
docs.text:
The furnace takes two inputs: resin in one, sulphur in the other. Fired together they cure into rubber.

  1. Cure resin and sulphur into rubber in the furnace. — have 4× Rubber

Rubber seals the airlocks, and makes a mat that springs.

docs.title: Leap of Faith
docs.text:
A rubber mat on four springs throws you back a little higher than you fell, up to five tiles. Jump as you land for a little more; hold S to stop.

  1. Build a Trampoline and jump on it. — build Trampoline

Opens: Trampoline

Up is a direction again.

docs.title: Precious Metals … Locker Five
docs.text: After Refinery.

docs.title: Precious Metals
docs.text:
Gold, silver and titanium lie deep, or come one grain in hundreds from the separator. The ship's last repairs need all three - and so do the best instruments.

  1. Smelt a gold, a silver and a titanium ingot. — have Gold Ingot; have Silver Ingot; have Titanium Ingot

Gold for contacts, silver for mirrors, titanium for the suit.

docs.title: Locker Five
docs.text:
Debris went through the tall locker in the hold. Nickel steel to patch it and a catalyst for its seal - the last of the ship's lockers.

  1. Repair the fifth locker at the console by the hatch, then right-click it and take what it holds. — have Rocket Launcher

The rocket launcher and the jetpack. Every locker in the ship is open.

docs.title: Open Every Locker
docs.text: After Salvage.

docs.title: Open Every Locker
docs.text:
The ship is the way off this planet. Everything broken in it has to be put right - its lockers first, its systems after.

  1. Repair every locker in the ship and take what each holds. — have Flamethrower; have Wrench; have Designator; have Rocket Launcher

Every locker is open. The ship's systems are next.

docs.title: Hands Off
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Hands Off
docs.text:
Deepcut's licence is paid for. Their drones dig and carry what you point at, so the hours you spent on a slope can go to something else. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Build the Drone Station from the catalogue. — stand Drone Station
  2. Mark loose ground or a pool in the station's range with the Designator. Its collector brings it in. — haul 200× Drone Station
  3. Buy a Miner Drone from Deepcut and put it into the station's cargo. It breaks the solid ground you mark. — dock Miner Drone

A miner to break the rock, a collector to bring it in: the ground you mark comes to the station by itself.

docs.title: Skin of the Ship
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Skin of the Ship
docs.text:
The roof is holed, the glass is cracked, the bow is gone. The hull is repaired at the console by the hatch, a layer at a time, and each layer wants a better plate than the last.

  1. Patch the roof with hull plate and wire: repair the Hull at the console by the hatch. — repair Hull
  2. Strap the glass with steel plate and insulated wire. — repair 2× Hull
  3. Close the breach with plasteel and nickel-steel plate. — repair 3× Hull
  4. Build the nose from composite panels: carbon fibre cured in resin in the autoclave. — repair 4× Hull

Composite over plasteel over steel: the hull will hold what the climb puts on it.

docs.title: Air to Breathe
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Air to Breathe
docs.text:
The ship's air is what the suit carried in. Life support starts with filters and a fan and ends with a membrane that takes the breath back out of the air.

  1. Fit filter cartridges and a fan: repair Life Support at the console by the hatch. — repair Life support
  2. Rebuild the life unit: iron pipe, a motor and rubber seals. — repair 2× Life support
  3. Fit the silver membranes that scrub the air. — repair 3× Life support

The cabin makes its own air now. Nobody has to hold their breath to orbit.

docs.title: Fire in the Pods
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Fire in the Pods
docs.text:
Four pods, none of them whole. The thrusters want steel and bearings, the rear pod nickel steel and coils, and the two in the middle want chambers that hold a flame steel cannot.

  1. Rebuild the thrusters with steel plate and bearings: repair the Engines at the console. — repair Engines
  2. Patch the rear pod with nickel-steel plate and coils. — repair 2× Engines
  3. Fit combustors, catalyst, motors and titanium to the middle pods. — repair 3× Engines

Every pod lights. What is left is something to burn in them.

docs.title: Lines and Tanks
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Lines and Tanks
docs.text:
Two tanks ride in the hull, one for hydrogen and one for oxygen, and neither holds anything until its lines are sound. Nothing can be loaded into a tank that is not repaired.

  1. Run copper pipe and rubber to the hydrogen valve: repair Fuel at the console. — repair Fuel
  2. Plate the hydrogen tank in steel and give it a glass gauge. — repair 2× Fuel
  3. Repair the Oxidiser: steel plate, copper pipe and a microchip. — repair Oxidiser

Both tanks are tight. They are also empty.

docs.title: Finding the Way
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Finding the Way
docs.text:
The antenna hears the system now, but hearing is not steering. The nav screen wants lenses and a display; the core that flies the ship cannot be made here at all - someone out there sells one.

  1. Rebuild the nav screen: lenses, a display and microchips. Repair Navigation at the console. — repair 2× Navigation
  2. Fit a navigation core bought from a corporation, with oscillators and gyroscopes. — repair 3× Navigation

The dash is lit from end to end. The ship knows where up is, and where it ends.

docs.title: Eyes on the Ground
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Eyes on the Ground
docs.text:
The survey dish came off its yoke in the crash and lies on the hold's roof. It was the miners' way of reading the rock under the ship. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Put the dish back: copper wire, a lens and a microchip. Repair the Radar at the console. — repair Radar
  2. Fit the ground reader: a display, microchips and coils. — repair 2× Radar
  3. Wake the deep array: displays, quartz oscillators and microchips. — repair 3× Radar

The array is awake, every stage of it. What it hears, it keeps to itself for now.

docs.title: Head of Steam
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Head of Steam
docs.text:
Panels sleep at night, and an arc furnace eats more than a roof of them gives. A boiler turns water and anything that burns into steam; a turbine turns the steam into power and hands the water back. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Place a Boiler and a Steam Turbine. Pipe the boiler's dome to the turbine's inlet, and the turbine's outlet back to the boiler's. — build Boiler; build Steam Turbine

The same water, round and round, and a wire that is live after dark.

docs.title: Deep Heat
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Deep Heat
docs.text:
Hydrogen and oxygen made the ship's fuel; across a silver membrane they make power instead, with no flame and water left over. The ground is warm for nothing wherever lava lies under it. And a night is long for an arc furnace. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Place a Fuel Cell. Pipe hydrogen into its left and oxygen into its top, and its water out of the right. — build Fuel Cell
  2. Make a Geothermal Tap at the Electrics Bench and stand it on rock over lava. The Visor shows how hot the ground under it is. — build Geothermal Tap
  3. Make an Accumulator at the Electrics Bench and wire it in. — build Accumulator

A wire that is live at midnight, with no fire anywhere on it.

docs.title: Switched On
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Switched On
docs.text:
The Wire Tool has a second mode. In it a wire carries no power, only yes or no: from a lever to a door, from a sensor to a pump, through an element that says the opposite. A base that is wired this way runs itself. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Make a Signal Lever at the Electrics Bench and place it. With the Wire Tool in hand press R for signal wires, click the lever and then a door or a lamp, and throw the lever with the right button. — build Signal Lever
  2. Place a Daylight Sensor and a NOT Element. Wire the sensor to the element and the element to a lamp: it lights at dusk. — build Daylight Sensor; build NOT Element
  3. Place a Fill Sensor near the top of a pit or a bin and wire it to whatever fills it, through a NOT Element: it stops when the bin is full. — build Fill Sensor

The door answers the lever, the lamp answers the dark, and nobody has to stand there.

docs.title: Keep a Stock
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Keep a Stock
docs.text:
A chest can say how much it holds. Wired to a station, it starts the work when the shelf runs low and stops it when the shelf is full. The datalog's Signal Schemes shows how. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Feed a Furnace by tube and let it put its ingots into a Chest. With the Wire Tool in signal mode, right-click the chest and set output A to "holds fewer than" a number of ingots, then wire A to the furnace. — wire Chest
  2. Let it run: the furnace smelts until the chest holds the number, and starts again when you take some out. — run 5× Furnace

The furnace works when the chest is short and rests when it is not. Nobody counts the ingots any more.

docs.title: Supply on Demand
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Supply on Demand
docs.text:
A silo with a wire on its input gives to the tubes only while the signal is on. A station can give that signal itself, when it has nothing left to work on. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Set the Furnace's output A to "lacks input" and wire it to the input of the Grain Silo that feeds it. — wire Furnace
  2. Set its output B to "works" and wire it to a Lamp: it lights while the furnace is busy. — wire Furnace

The silo sends ore only when the furnace asks for it, and a lamp tells you when it is running.

docs.title: Exactly Forty
docs.text: After Air Works.

docs.title: Exactly Forty
docs.text:
A Counter Tube set to Stop lets a number through and no more until it is reset. A button on its reset measures out a batch at a press, and a display shows how far the batch has got. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Make a Counter Tube at the Aero Workshop and put it into an aero line. In its panel set the number and choose Stop. — build Counter Tube
  2. Wire a Signal Button to the counter's reset, and the counter to a Text Display with {n} in its text. — wire Signal Button; wire Counter Tube

A press, forty, and the line stands. The display says when the batch is whole.

docs.title: Power to Spare
docs.text: The first quest.

docs.title: Power to Spare
docs.text:
The Wire Tool lay in the fourth locker for a reason. Silicon cells turn daylight into power, a bank of cells keeps it through the night, and a machine wired to them works faster for as long as there is charge. Nothing here is needed to leave the planet.

  1. Wind two Wire Spools at the assembler: four insulated wires each. — have 2× Wire Spool
  2. Place a Solar Panel under an open sky and a Battery Bank within 16 m of it. With the Wire Tool in hand, click the panel and then the bank. — build Solar Panel; build Battery Bank

The bank's lamps climb through the day. Whatever is wired to it runs faster while they are lit.

docs.text:
Rocket Launcher Category Explosives Hotbar label RL Charges 3, one back every 4 s

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: A signal wire carries nothing but on or off. It runs from an output to an input, costs nothing and reaches as far as you like. Press R with the Wire Tool in hand to see the signal wires and lay them; point at a port and its own wires light up, wherever they run.

docs.title: How a wire works
docs.text:
1. An output is a filled square, an input a hollow one. A wire goes from an output to an input, never the other way, and never to a power connector.
  2. An input is on while any wire into it is on - two wires into one input are "either".
  3. What a wire reaches obeys it and not your hand: a door, a hatch or an airlock opens, a valve opens, a lamp lights, a pump, a fan, an intake and a heater run, a station works, and a chest or a silo lets the tubes take from it. Cut the wire and it is yours again.
  4. Every element answers a tick late, so a NOT wired back to itself blinks rather than hangs.

docs.title: Four outputs, four colours
docs.text:
A Chest, a Grain Silo, a tank, a battery and every station have four outputs - A red, B green, C blue, D yellow - each on by a condition of its own:

  • a chest or a silo: at least / less than N percent full, holds fewer than / at least N of a thing, empty, full;
  • a tank or a battery: at least / less than N percent full, empty, full;
  • a station: it works, it lacks input, its output is full.

Each output either holds while its condition is true or gives one short pulse when it becomes true. An output has a port only while it has a condition. A wire takes the colour of the output it leaves, so a plant reads at a glance. Set them in the signal window - the right button with the Wire Tool in signal mode, or the lamp in a chest's or a silo's window; its left column says what each output does and where its wires go.

A lever, a sensor, a logic element, a timer, a Counter Tube and a display have one output each, in a colour you choose in its panel. The right button on a wired valve turns it to be open while the signal is off.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text: Machine What it does How to get it Signal Lever A lever on a plate, one tile. made at Electrics Bench Signal Button A push button on a plate, one tile. made at Electrics Bench Presence Sensor An eye on a plate, one tile. made at Electrics Bench Daylight Sensor A light cell on a plate, one tile. made at Electrics Bench Thermometer Sensor A thermometer on a plate, one tile, with no body: set it into what is to be measured. made at Electrics Bench Fill Sensor A mesh plate set like a back wall, one tile, with no body: sand, ore and liquid pass through it and pile over it. made at Electrics Bench Signal Timer A clock on a plate, one tile. made at Electrics Bench NOT Element A logic element, one tile: its output is on while its input is off. made at Electrics Bench AND Element A logic element, one tile, with two inputs, A and B: its output is on only while both are on. made at Electrics Bench Latch Element A logic element, one tile, that remembers. made at Electrics Bench Delay Element A logic element, one tile: its output follows its input, but only once the input has held for the time set in its panel. made at Electrics Bench Counter Tube A tube segment that counts what passes through it and gives a signal at a number you set. made at Aero Workshop Text Display A screen four tiles wide that shows a line of your text, ten characters, and glows in the dark. made at Electrics Bench Display Board A screen four tiles wide and two high: your caption on top and under it the number, twice the size, read from across a hall. made at Electrics Bench

docs.title: Keep a stock
docs.text:
Keep a stock: the chest's output A, "holds fewer than 20 Iron Ingot", runs the furnace and the display.

The chest's output A is "holds fewer than 20 Iron Ingot", wired to the furnace and to a Text Display. The furnace smelts while the chest is short and stands once it holds twenty; take some out and it starts again. The display shows the count, in red while the stock is low.

docs.title: Supply on demand
docs.text:
Supply on demand: the furnace's A, "lacks input", opens the silo; its B, "works", lights a lamp.

The furnace's output A is "lacks input", wired to the silo of ore and a lamp; B is "works", wired to a second lamp. A silo with a wire on its input gives to the tubes only while the signal is on, so ore comes only when the furnace runs out and the line is never choked with a whole silo.

docs.title: Overflow
docs.text:
Overflow: at 90% the main silo's A shuts the turned valve and opens the other - the rest goes to the spare silo.

The main silo's output A is "at least 90% full", wired to both valves behind an Aero Splitter. The valve to the main silo is turned to open while the signal is off. Cargo fills the main silo, then goes to the spare one - one wire, and the turned valve does the NOT.

docs.title: Exactly forty at a press
docs.text:
Exactly forty at a press: a Counter Tube set to Stop at 40, a button on its reset.

A Counter Tube set to Stop at 40, a button on its reset, a display on its output. Forty pass and the line stands; a press lets forty more go. A Filter before the counter measures out one thing.

docs.title: An alarm that remembers
docs.text:
An alarm that remembers: the chest's B, "is empty" as a pulse, sets a latch that holds a lamp on.

The chest's output B is "is empty", as a pulse, wired to a latch's set; a button on its reset, a lamp on its output. The lamp lights the moment the chest runs dry and stays lit until the button is pressed - a shortage you were not there for still shows.

Every signal piece is made at the Electrics Bench.

docs.title: Working a station
docs.text:
A station turns one thing into another: the Furnace smelts ore, the Crusher breaks rock down, the Workbench fits parts together. They all work the same way, through the same window.

Right-click a placed station to open it.

A furnace worked by hand: a recipe picked, ore and coal dragged in from the carried tanks, Max, Craft, and the ingots come out.

docs.title: The window, left to right
docs.text:
1. Pick a recipe in the list on the left. The squares in the middle become that recipe: what goes in, the fuel if the station burns any, an arrow, what comes out.
  2. Set how many in the number field. Every square then says how much of its ingredient that count needs.
  3. Load it. Drag a carried tank from Heavy onto an input to pour it in, drag items from the backpack, or use the small buttons under a square — they take exactly what the count needs from everything you carry. An empty square shows faintly what it is waiting for.
  4. Press Craft — the gear. The arrow fills as the station works, and the result lands in the output squares. The button beside the count sets it to as many as the station can run with what is loaded.
  5. Take the result by dragging it into the backpack.

A station keeps working with its window shut, and keeps what it holds until you take it. What an earlier recipe left behind is shown apart and can be sent back to where it came from.

The furnace's window with a recipe chosen and two carried tanks to load from.

docs.title: Fuel
docs.text: Only a station with a flue burns fuel — the furnace does, a bench does not. Anything on the Fuels page will do; a stronger fuel does more work per cell.

docs.title: Letting it run by itself
docs.text:
Every station has ports for Aero tubes: inputs, an output, and a fuel input on the ones that burn.

  • Aero output — on, the result leaves by the tube on the output port; off, the station keeps it.
  • Auto-craft — the station starts the recipe again whenever its inputs are there. It needs a tube on the output first, so the results have somewhere to go.

Liquids arrive by Pipes and pumps and leave the same way.

Which station makes what: Machines by category; every recipe is on its station's own page.

docs.title: Trading
docs.text: Everything is traded through the Merchant Landing Pad: call a trader down, and it buys what stands on the pad and puts what you buy there. Nothing passes hand to hand.

docs.title: Calling a trader
docs.text:
The pad's window calls anyone or, once you have met one, a corporation by name. A call to anyone goes unanswered 20% of the time — never the very first call of a world — and whoever answers you have now met. A corporation at Enemy answers its name only 25% of the time. After a lander leaves, or nobody answers, the pad waits 120 seconds before it can call again.

The lander comes down only onto an open sky over the deck, takes 5 seconds to land, and stays until you send it away. Right-click its console for the trader's terminal: Trade, Contracts and Talk.

docs.title: The pad's cargo
docs.text: The pad holds up to 10,000 cells of material in any mix and 8 slots of items, with 2 upgrade slots for storage modules, each opening 8 more (up to 24). Load it by hand from carried tanks, through the aero port with a tube, or through the pipe port with a pump.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
Each corporation thinks of you somewhere from -1000 to 1000, in 10 bands. The better the band, the less a trader asks and the more it pays, the more of its stock it shows, and the better its contracts. Below Distrustful it will not trade at all — it only lands. The figures are shares of what a thing is worth:

Band Reputation You buy at You sell at Alliance Supply Service: buy / sell Enemy -1000 to -801 no trade no trade no trade Hostile -800 to -601 no trade no trade no trade Distrustful -600 to -401 149% 41% 171% / 29% Wary -400 to -201 143% 47% 167% / 32% Cold -200 to -1 138% 52% 162% / 34% Neutral 0 to 199 132% 58% 158% / 36% Acquainted 200 to 399 127% 63% 153% / 38% Trusted 400 to 599 121% 69% 149% / 41% Ally 600 to 799 116% 74% 144% / 43% Friend 800 to 1000 110% 80% 140% / 45%

docs.title: Stock, purse and plenty
docs.text:
A trader's stock and its purse — 20,000 credits it can pay out — are restocked every 3 days. Selling one corporation the same thing again and again lowers its price: 1,000 cells of a material, or 50 items or constructions of a kind, halve it, never below 30% of the price — until the restock.

Each corporation pays more for some kinds of thing and less for others; its page says which.

docs.title: Washer
docs.text:
Washer Category Crafting Size 3×3 tiles Input slots 2 Burns fuel no Tube ports in, out Pipe ports 2

A sluice that washes loose ground for the ore hidden in it. Send any loose ground by aero tube to the port on the upper left and pipe water into the lower left inlet; ore concentrate leaves by the aero port on the upper right, and the dirty water - about half of what went in - through the pipe at the lower right. With nowhere for the dirty water to go it stops. It burns no fuel.

docs.text:

A filter column that runs dirty water clean through sand, charcoal and gravel. Pipe dirty water into the lower left inlet and send filter cartridges by aero tube to the port above it; clean water leaves through the pipe on the right. One cartridge cleans 300 cells. It burns no fuel. Its second recipe makes brine: clean water by the pipe and salt by the aero tube. Salt poured into any pool of water dissolves into brine where it lies, too.

docs.title: Wire Tool
docs.text:
Wire Tool Category Construction Hotbar label WT

Lays the wires of a power network, and is the only way to see them: wires show while it is in hand. Left-click a connector, then another, to lay a wire between them - one Wire Spool a wire, up to 16 m, and it carries on from the last one. Right-click drops the wire in hand, or cuts the wire under the pointer and gives the spool back. A green mark is where energy goes in, an orange one where it comes out.

docs.title: The world
docs.text:
The world is one long slice of a planet, seen side-on. It runs from a frozen west through a green centre, where you land, to a desert east, with an ocean at each end. Below the ground the climate carries on downwards: each column of the world has its own layers of rock, caves, lakes and ores, getting harder, hotter and richer the deeper you dig, until a sealed band of basalt closes off the lava at the bottom.

A whole world of the middle size, west on the left.

docs.title: Sizes
docs.text:
You pick one of three sizes when you create a world. Every depth on these pages is measured from the zero line — a row 38% of the way down — as a share of the rock below it, so all three sizes keep the same layers.

Size Cells Zero line (row from the top) Underground (cells below it) Small 4,096 × 2,400 900 1,500 Medium 11,200 × 3,600 1,350 2,250 Large 16,000 × 5,000 1,875 3,125

docs.title: On the surface
docs.text:
West to east, three biomes; their edges are ragged, not ruled lines, and an ocean 8% of the world wide closes each end.

Biome Where Ground Climate Hills Caves Winter west Frozen Earth over Permafrost -20 °C ×3.6 ×1.1 Central centre Dirt over Dirt 20 °C ×1 ×1.25 Desert east Sand over Sandstone 57 °C ×0.6 ×0.55

Hills and caves are multipliers on the world's own: higher is more mountainous, more cave.

docs.title: Underground
docs.text:
The climate carries on below the surface, and the rock is laid in layers by depth. The table is read top to bottom and the first row that fits a place wins.

docs.title: Wrench
docs.text:
Wrench Category Construction

Takes a placed machine back into the inventory with one left click; R switches to painting, where a held stroke takes every empty machine it passes. Whatever it was holding - a station's ore and fuel, a chest's items, a silo's load - is left on the ground; a tank is carried whole, contents and all. The cursor is a wrench: in colour over anything it can take, grey elsewhere.
